papers.title: Impact of Circadian Adaptation on Sleep Architecture and Neurobehavioral Performance in Simulated Shiftwork.
papers.summary: In an 8-day simulated shiftwork protocol with 19 participants, greater circadian adaptation (measured by change in dim light melatonin onset) correlated with higher total sleep time, REM sleep, and sleep efficiency, and less wake after sleep onset, while more slow-wave sleep correlated with better neurobehavioral performance and less sleepiness. The authors conclude that interventions promoting circadian adaptation, such as timed light exposure, could improve sleep and performance in shiftworkers.

papers.title: Hemodynamic spectral signatures across vigilance states: a whole-night EEG/fNIRS investigation.
papers.summary: This study combined whole-night polysomnography, EEG, and personalized dense bilateral frontoparietal fNIRS in healthy young adults, plus an independent sleep EEG-fMRI dataset, to characterize cortical hemodynamic spectral signatures across vigilance states. Slow-frequency (0.002-0.1 Hz) HbO power rose in N1 and attenuated across N2/N3 in HbO, HbR, and fMRI, REM showed re-emergence of very-low-frequency (<0.01 Hz) power, and higher-frequency (0.15-0.5 Hz) oscillations were enhanced during NREM sleep.

papers.title: Acoustic stimuli-enhanced environmental enrichment remodulates cortical processing of sound azimuth in adult female rats.
papers.summary: In adult female rats, acoustic stimuli-enhanced environmental enrichment improved sound-azimuth discrimination and enhanced azimuth selectivity of primary auditory cortex neurons, accompanied by increased density of cortical parvalbumin-labeled inhibitory interneurons. Enrichment without extra sound exposure produced weaker but similar effects, indicating an additional contribution of acoustic stimulation to experience-dependent plasticity in the mature auditory cortex.

papers.title: Effects of Ambulatory Blood Pressure Monitoring During Polysomnography on Sleep Indices and EEG Power.
papers.summary: In a balanced two-night crossover of 72 nominally healthy adults with ABPM on one randomly assigned night, both ABPM and first-night effect were associated with lower composite sleep quality index, with ABPM linked to higher light-sleep and lower N3-sleep percentages and higher whole-night relative theta power. Of 655 ABPM measurements beginning during sleep, 60.3% contained at least one arousal detection within the 2-min window.

papers.title: MM-SleepNet: An Automatic Sleep Staging Network Based on Modal Re-Weighting and Mamba.
papers.summary: The paper proposes MM-SleepNet, an automatic sleep staging network that splits epochs into overlapping patches, uses a dynamic modal re-weighting module to weight EEG/EOG signals per patch, and applies a bidirectional Mamba encoder with positional encoding for cross-epoch context. On Sleep-EDF and ISRUC it reportedly outperformed state-of-the-art methods, with ablations demonstrating the effectiveness of its modules.

papers.title: Repairing the disruption of protein homeostasis ameliorates REM sleep dysfunction in mouse models of Huntington's disease.
papers.summary: Huntington's disease mice showed REM sleep impairments and protein aggregation in sleep-related regions including the nucleus accumbens and amygdala, and augmenting selective autophagy in the brain slowed aberrant protein accumulation and ameliorated REM sleep deficits. The findings suggest that disrupted protein homeostasis contributes to sleep dysfunction in Huntington's disease models.

papers.title: Using hip-worn accelerometer non-wear time to assess sleep duration and sleep midpoint.
papers.summary: Using hip-worn accelerometer non-wear time as a proxy for time in bed in 17,855 Cancer Prevention Study-3 participants, sleep duration showed convergent validity with sleep diaries (r = 0.72 weekdays, r = 0.67 weekends) though time in bed was about 41 minutes longer than diary estimates, and sleep midpoint was equivalent to diary within ±15 minutes. The authors propose that previously collected hip accelerometry data can be leveraged to estimate sleep duration and midpoint.

papers.title: Revisiting EEG slowing in isolated REM sleep behavior disorder: rhythms, background, and phenoconversion.
papers.summary: The supplied record provides a title on EEG slowing in isolated REM sleep behavior disorder in relation to rhythms, background, and phenoconversion, but no abstract or findings are available, so no concrete result can be reported.

papers.title: Effects of BL Exposure on Circadian Rhythms and Rhythm-Related Disorders.
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes evidence on the bidirectional effects of blue light (BL) exposure on circadian rhythms and related disorders, outlining molecular mechanisms and disease pathways. It highlights that inappropriately timed BL may disrupt circadian rhythms and contribute to sleep, mood, and neurodegenerative disorders, while appropriately timed BL interventions may improve circadian alignment, though causal pathways remain unestablished.

papers.title: The Circadian Diet in Age-Related Neurodegeneration: Nutrient Timing, Sleep, and Mitochondrial Mechanisms.
papers.summary: This narrative review examines chrononutrition in age-related neurodegeneration, integrating evidence from cellular, animal, and human studies on meal timing, sleep, and mitochondrial mechanisms. It concludes that while experimental findings provide mechanistic plausibility, metabolic improvements have not translated into demonstrated neuroprotection, and adequately powered trials are needed before a circadian diet can be established as disease-modifying.

papers.title: Interoceptive-autonomic pathways in mood state transitions in bipolar disorder: a hypothesis-generating brief review.
papers.summary: This hypothesis-generating review proposes a state-dependent framework linking sleep-circadian disruption, autonomic flexibility, interoceptive processing, and emotion regulation to mood-state transitions in bipolar disorder, distinguishing cross-sectional correlates from longitudinal predictors. It outlines a research protocol combining state-stratified heartbeat discrimination tasks, HRV reactivity/recovery, sleep-activity rhythms, and ecological momentary assessment, while stressing that temporal sequence and causal contributions remain unestablished.

papers.title: Epilepsy at the Airport.
papers.summary: This retrospective study reviewed 242 Epilepsy Rapid Access Clinic attendees over 19 months and identified 18 patients with air travel-related seizures, all bilateral tonic-clonic, with clustering in departure terminals particularly before morning flights and sleep deprivation as a common trigger. The findings suggest that patients with idiopathic generalised epilepsy may be at higher risk and that targeted counselling on modifiable risk factors could reduce risk.

papers.title: Contactless Oxygen Desaturation Prediction and Oxygen Desaturation Index (ODI) Estimation from Nocturnal Breathing Sounds via Deep Learning.
papers.summary: Developed a contactless Vision Transformer-based deep learning model trained on 2,973 nights of synchronized polysomnography and audio to detect oxygen desaturation events from nocturnal breathing sounds. Epoch-level detection reached sensitivity 0.79, specificity 0.95, accuracy 0.92, and κ 0.74, with estimated ODI correlating strongly with PSG-derived ODI (r = 0.93).

papers.title: The Case for Low-Friction High-Adherence Passive Sleep-Tracking Devices in Longitudinal Monitoring of Neurodegenerative Disease.
papers.summary: This perspective argues that low-friction, high-adherence passive sleep-tracking devices, such as smart rings, may offer advantages for longitudinal monitoring of neurodegenerative diseases like Parkinson's despite lower accuracy than gold-standard methods. It posits that long-term statistical benefits from detecting within-person changes and increased sampling frequency may offset accuracy-adherence trade-offs.

papers.title: Integrating Chronophysiological and Bioinformatic Perspectives on Nesfatin-1, Circadian Feeding Rhythms, and Cortisol Regulation.
papers.summary: This review integrates chronophysiological and bioinformatic perspectives on nesfatin-1, circadian feeding rhythms, and cortisol regulation, synthesizing rodent and cell studies and performing in silico protein-association analysis. It identifies an evidence gap regarding the 24-hour temporal profile of nesfatin-1 in humans and its phase relationship with cortisol, calling for controlled time-resolved human studies.

papers.title: Cannabinol for Sleep and Insomnia: A Critical Narrative Review and an Olive-Derived Polyphenol Combination Hypothesis.
papers.summary: This critical narrative review evaluated CBN-specific sleep trials and found that primary sleep-quality and sleep-maintenance outcomes were not consistently positive, with dose-ranging signals multiplicity-sensitive and no optimal dose identified; at 300 mg, an acute insomnia trial showed selected secondary sleep benefits alongside next-day vigilance and simulated-driving concerns. It proposed an olive-derived polyphenol combination only as an untested hypothesis requiring exposure-informed investigation, not therapeutic endorsement.

papers.title: Choroid plexus volume as a marker of chronotherapeutic responsiveness in major depressive disorder.
papers.summary: In 25 MDD patients and 25 matched controls, total sleep deprivation plus light therapy reduced depressive symptoms and improved sleep quality, and treatment responders showed larger baseline left choroid plexus volume plus post-treatment reductions in choroid plexus volume that predicted clinical improvement. The findings suggest choroid plexus volume as a biomarker of chronotherapeutic responsiveness and circadian realignment in MDD.

papers.title: Detecting sleep deprivation from running biomechanics using machine learning classification: a comparison between wearable and laboratory motion capture.
papers.summary: Using a randomized crossover design with 21 recreational runners, machine learning classifiers detected total sleep deprivation from running biomechanics with best within-subject accuracies of 84% for a trunk-mounted wearable and 81% for laboratory motion capture, whereas between-subject classification stayed near chance (~50%). Both systems identified temporal organization, loading-related variables, and stride-to-stride variability as the most discriminative feature domains.

papers.title: Scalp high-frequency oscillations differentiate neonates with hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy with and without electroencephalographically confirmed seizures.
papers.summary: Retrospectively analyzing routine scalp EEG from 33 term neonates with hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy, the authors found significantly higher automated HFO rates in neonates with seizures versus without (0.12 vs 0.03 HFOs/min/channel; adjusted p = .02), with a 0.07 threshold yielding AUC 0.81. HFO rate was the strongest contributor in multivariable models incorporating EEG background and MRI findings.

papers.title: EEG Microstate Alterations and Their Association with Cognitive Performance in Late-Onset Epilepsy of Unknown Etiology: Comparison with Alzheimer's Disease.
papers.summary: Compared resting-state EEG microstate dynamics in 60 patients with late-onset epilepsy of unknown etiology (LOEU), 65 with Alzheimer's disease (AD), and 60 cognitively normal controls, finding longer microstate B duration and lower microstate C occurrence in both patient groups versus controls and longer microstate D duration in LOEU than in AD or controls. In LOEU, longer microstate A duration was associated with lower MoCA and MMSE scores, supporting EEG microstates as electrophysiological correlates of cognitive dysfunction.

papers.title: White matter microstructure and hyperintensity burden in isolated REM sleep behaviour disorder.
papers.summary: Analyzed multi-shell diffusion MRI (DTI and NODDI) and white matter hyperintensity burden across 39 white matter regions in 168 polysomnography-confirmed isolated REM sleep behaviour disorder participants from the North American Prodromal Synucleinopathy Consortium, comparing clinically impaired and unimpaired individuals. White matter hyperintensity burden was higher in impaired participants and showed broader associations with cognition, motor, olfactory, autonomic, and prodromal severity measures than diffusion microstructure metrics, highlighting cerebrovascular burden as a key correlate of clinical dysfunction.

papers.title: Postoperative Delirium Across the Perioperative Pathway: A Structured Narrative Review of Clinical Maturity and Implementation Priorities.
papers.summary: Structured narrative review synthesizing evidence on postoperative delirium across the perioperative pathway, classifying prevention and treatment strategies by clinical maturity. Reports that multicomponent non-pharmacological prevention has the most consistent support, while no single anesthetic technique, EEG target, blood-pressure threshold, or pharmacological agent consistently prevents POD.

papers.title: EEG Biomarkers for Stress Detection: A Comparative Analysis of Hjorth Parameters, Spectral and Fractal-Dimension Measures.
papers.summary: Comparative machine-learning analysis of pre-recorded EEG data from a stress-inducing experiment evaluating Hjorth parameters, spectral features, and fractal-dimension measures for stress classification. Hjorth activity, frontal beta asymmetry, and the gamma/theta ratio were among the most frequently selected features, and combined feature spaces outperformed conventional spectral features alone.

papers.title: Circadian Rhythm-Related Characteristics and Adiposity in Relation to CAP-Defined Hepatic Steatosis Among Shift and Non-Shift Workers: A Pilot Study.
papers.summary: In a pilot study of 436 tea-factory workers, CAP-defined hepatic steatosis and CAP values did not differ significantly by shift-work status, and CAP was strongly correlated with anthropometric and adiposity indices (e.g., waist circumference, abdominal volume index, BMI, body fat mass; all rs = 0.66). Social jetlag, eating jetlag, sleep duration, and PSQI score were not independently associated with CAP, and waist circumference/AVI discriminated steatosis best in men while BMI performed best in women.

papers.title: Associations of short and long sleep duration with multiple adverse health outcomes among ageing adults in South Africa.
papers.summary: Used three waves (2015-2022) of the HAALSI longitudinal cohort of South African adults aged 40 and older to examine associations of short and long sleep duration with multiple adverse health outcomes. Short sleep duration was associated with four outcomes (mortality, hypertension, depressive symptoms, cardiovascular disease) and long sleep duration with nine (including functional limitations, loneliness, PTSD symptoms, impaired cognition, dynapenia, and obesity measures).

papers.title: Simultaneous EEG-fMRI in major depressive disorder: A systematic review of brain networks, neurovascular coupling, and clinical correlates.
papers.summary: Systematic review (PRISMA 2020) of simultaneous EEG-fMRI studies restricted to strictly defined adult major depressive disorder, synthesizing nine studies (eight cohorts; N=377) on brain networks, neurovascular coupling, and clinical correlates. Moderate-to-strong correlations were reported for anhedonia (r=0.47 and 0.69) in neurofeedback studies, but heterogeneity and low certainty evidence precluded generalizable resting-state biomarkers.

papers.title: Short-term physiological responses to nocturnal pressurization in male high-altitude workers: an exploratory pilot randomized controlled trial.
papers.journal: International archives of occupational and environmental health
papers.summary: Exploratory pilot randomized controlled trial in 24 male high-altitude workers comparing nocturnal pressurization simulating altitude reduction during sleep versus control over five weeks. The intervention increased nocturnal SpO2 at 2500 m and 2000 m, lowered nocturnal diastolic BP at 2500 m, and reduced normetanephrine, metanephrine, angiotensin II, and oxidative stress markers at 2000 m, with all changes reversible one week after cessation.

papers.title: Spontaneous Parturition at Term Is Governed by Endogenous Circadian Rhythms Rather Than Geophysical or Meteorological Factors: A Historical Cohort Study.
papers.summary: Historical cohort study of 21,538 spontaneous term singleton deliveries (1998-2022) testing lunar phase, barometric pressure, and heat associations with labor onset and premature rupture of membranes. No lunar or meteorological effects were found, whereas spontaneous deliveries showed a robust endogenous circadian peak at midday.

papers.title: Thermally provoked itch in atopic dermatitis: current evidence, knowledge gaps, and digital approaches to nocturnal scratching.
papers.summary: This narrative review examines the clinical relevance, mechanistic evidence, and objective digital monitoring of thermally provoked itch in atopic dermatitis. It argues that thermosensitive ion channels, epithelial cytokines, neuropeptides, and artemin form a plausible mechanistic framework, but human evidence remains incomplete, and that wearable and non-wearable digital tools can add an objective behavioral layer for quantifying nocturnal scratching without replacing patient-reported outcomes.

papers.title: Stress, Depression, and Purpose-Specific Use of Dietary Supplements and Over-the-Counter Preparations: A Cross-Sectional Study of 120,000 Polish Adults.
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional web survey of 120,000 Polish adults, purpose-specific supplement/OTC use (mood, sleep, memory) rose along a gradient of psychological burden, with lifetime depression diagnosis associated with mood-product use (aOR 2.53) and OTC self-medication without reduced primary-care contact. Multivitamin and hair/skin use stayed flat, and associations replicated across age and sex strata (E-values 4.3–9.5).

papers.title: Lesion-directed quantitative EEG after reperfusion therapy is associated with malignant cerebral edema and functional outcomes in acute ischemic stroke: a prospective exploratory cohort study.
papers.summary: In a prospective cohort of 49 anterior-circulation ischemic stroke patients, a lesion-directed alpha-to-delta ratio measured within 72 h after reperfusion was associated with functional outcomes, and combined with EEG timing showed good discrimination for malignant cerebral edema (optimism-corrected AUC 0.889). The association with 90-day independence was attenuated after adjusting for admission NIHSS.

papers.title: EEG-Based Recognition of Self-Imagined Emotions Using Multi-Domain Features and Subject-Specific Calibration.
papers.summary: This study evaluated a multi-domain EEG decoding framework combining time-frequency, functional and effective connectivity features with subject-specific calibration for recognizing four self-imagined emotions in 38 participants. PLV-based SVM features reached 97.0% accuracy under pooled cross-validation and 95.0% with 75% target-subject calibration, but leave-one-subject-out accuracy fell to 25-30%, indicating limited cross-subject generalization.

papers.title: A Lightweight Hybrid-Attention Conformer for Affective State Recognition from Wearable EEG.
papers.summary: The authors propose KimiFormer, a lightweight hybrid-attention Conformer that classifies raw wearable EEG, using a spatio-temporal stemming module and combined linear/full attention. It achieved 95.5% accuracy on the EEG Violence Dataset (97.0% under 10-fold CV) with 3.2M parameters and 15.64 ms latency, but subject-independent performance on the external DREAMER dataset remained near chance.

papers.title: Correction: Caffeine and modafinil ameliorate the neuroinflammation and anxious behavior in rats during sleep deprivation by inhibiting the microglia activation.
papers.summary: This is a published erratum correcting an earlier article on caffeine and modafinil ameliorating neuroinflammation and anxious behavior in sleep-deprived rats via inhibition of microglial activation. It contains no new findings beyond the correction notice.

papers.title: [Digital media use and dependencies in adolescence: Psychological and mental health perspectives, regulatory dilemmas, and preventive considerations].
papers.journal: Psychiatria Hungarica : A Magyar Pszichiatriai Tarsasag tudomanyos folyoirata
papers.summary: This narrative and integrative review synthesizes international and Hungarian literature on adolescent problematic digital media use, framing it as a developmental, social-psychological, and mental health environment rather than mere frequency of use. It emphasizes loss of control, functional impairment, and outsourced affect regulation, links problematic use to depressive and anxiety symptoms, poorer sleep, attentional instability, and social comparison, and recommends coordinated platform, family, school, digital-literacy, and early-clinical prevention approaches.

papers.title: The association between physical activity and academic procrastination among college students: the mediating role of self-efficacy and the moderating role of sleep quality.
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional survey of 428 Shanghai college students, this study tested a moderated mediation model linking physical activity to academic procrastination via self-efficacy and moderated by sleep quality. Physical activity was negatively associated with procrastination and positively with self-efficacy, self-efficacy partially mediated the association (indirect effect -0.047, 27.01% of the total effect), and sleep quality moderated both the physical activity–self-efficacy and direct physical activity–procrastination paths, with effects present only among students with average or good sleep quality.

papers.title: Correction: The impact of sleep deprivation on cognitive function in healthy adults: insights from auditory P300 and reaction time analysis.
papers.summary: This is a published erratum correcting an earlier article on sleep deprivation and cognitive function in healthy adults assessed with auditory P300 and reaction time analysis. It reports only a correction and no new results.

papers.title: Translating Geroscience Into Clinical Practice: Molecular Targets, Emerging Therapies, and Lifestyle Strategies for Healthy Longevity.
papers.summary: Critical narrative review synthesizing molecular geroscience, experimental therapeutics, biomarkers, and lifestyle factors for healthy longevity, framed within an expanded 12-hallmark aging network. It concludes that geroprotectors such as senolytics, NAD+ augmentation, mTOR inhibition, metformin, and spermidine lack definitive evidence for lifespan extension in healthy humans, whereas fitness, strength, diet quality, sleep, and cardiometabolic risk management have stronger human-outcome support.

papers.title: Acupuncture-Assisted Zolpidem Tartrate Tapering and Discontinuation in Patients with Chronic Insomnia Disorder Stabilized on Zolpidem: A Study Protocol for a Randomized Controlled Trial.
papers.summary: Protocol for a single-center, single-blind randomized controlled trial randomizing 90 chronic insomnia disorder patients stable on zolpidem 1:1 to acupuncture or sham acupuncture alongside zolpidem tapering over 8 weeks with 4-week follow-up. The primary outcome is the zolpidem discontinuation rate at week 8, with secondary outcomes including taper reduction rates, Insomnia Severity Index, anxiety/depression scales, and sleep diary measures.

papers.title: Promotion and economic considerations of domestic Vagus nerve stimulation within the Chinese three-tier epilepsy center system.
papers.summary: Narrative synthesis of clinical outcomes, promotion pathways, and economic considerations for domestic vagus nerve stimulation within the Chinese three-tier epilepsy center network, drawing on real-world studies of 124 adults and 87 children with drug-resistant epilepsy. Adult responder rates rose from 35.4% at 1 month to 76.6% at 12 months with 10.9% seizure-free, pediatric responder rates ranged roughly 40–57%, and comorbid sleep, depression, anxiety, and quality-of-life measures improved with mild transient adverse events.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
